title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
summary_box: At the 2026-11-13 ledger close of ₹311.30 (₹2,086 Cr MCap on 6.70 Cr shares; post-cutoff 2026-11-16 quote ₹292.45), INDIAGLYCO's headline 9.27x P/E (6.0x on TradingView) is a pre-demerger accounting mirage. It embeds Dec 2025 and Mar 2026 profits from carved-out Potable Spirits and Ennature Biopharma. Continuing operations run at ₹1,438 Cr annualized revenue, 11% OPM, ₹114 Cr headline PAT (12.31% effective tax; 52.3% PBT from Other Income/JV), and ₹97.5 Cr tax-normalized PAT at 25% tax (₹14.53 EPS). On that clean perimeter, the stock trades at 18.5x headline continuing P/E (21.4x tax-normalized) and 14.2x–16.0x EV/EBITDA (ex-investments), with a ₹211 bear-case floor.

epigraph.quote: A low trailing multiple after a corporate split is often a rear-view mirror bolted onto a brand-new chassis; you only know what you are paying when you price the engine that stayed in the car.
epigraph.author: Special-Situations Valuation Maxim

web_blocks.html: On a standard retail screener today, India Glycols Limited (INDIAGLYCO) looks almost absurdly cheap [1][23]. At the 2026-11-13 ledger close of ₹311.30, market capitalization is ₹2,086 Cr on 6.70 Cr shares [1][23]. Meanwhile, Screener's post-cutoff 2026-11-16 feed displays a trailing Stock P/E of 9.27x (6.0x on TradingView, at a separate post-session quote of ₹292.45, -6.06%) [1][23]. In an Indian specialty-chemical universe where peers routinely trade between 15x and 26x earnings, a single-digit P/E triggers value-hunter instincts. Before committing a single rupee on that assumption, we must dismantle that trailing P/E. We need to rebuild the valuation strictly on the post-demerger continuing perimeter [2][4].

Why is the 9.27x multiple an accounting mirage? Trailing twelve-month (TTM) earnings as of September 2026 still include two full pre-demerger quarters [1][13][14]. Q3 FY26 (Dec 2025) delivered ₹1,102 Cr sales, ₹175 Cr operating profit, and ₹68 Cr PAT, while Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) delivered ₹976 Cr sales, ₹166 Cr operating profit, and ₹87 Cr PAT. During those quarters, the high-margin Potable Spirits & Bio-Fuels engine (~21% EBIT margin) and Ennature Biopharma were still inside the consolidated P&L. Under the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Appointed Date April 1, 2026; Effective Date September 1, 2026), both undertakings moved out into standalone entities [2][3][8]. What remains in listed INDIAGLYCO is Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC), Industrial Gases, and the 49% equity stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals [2][10][11].

web_blocks.takeaway: Once stripped of pre-demerger spirits earnings and normalized for tax, INDIAGLYCO at ₹311.30 trades at 18.5x headline (21.42x tax-normalized) P/E and 14.2x–16.0x EV/EBITDA (ex-investments)—a full specialty-chemical multiple [1][4].

web_blocks.html: This perimeter reset changes the entire investment framing [1][4]. At 18.5x headline continuing earnings (21.4x tax-normalized) and 14.2x–16.0x EV/EBITDA (ex-investments), the market is not giving away the chemical business for free. To see exactly what ₹311.30 embeds, let us run a Reverse DCF on the continuing entity [1][10]. We use a 12.0% cost of equity / WACC, a 4.5% terminal growth rate, ₹1,438 Cr starting revenue, and ₹826 Cr gross debt offset by ₹422 Cr in JV investments. Justifying a ₹2,086 Cr equity valuation requires two things simultaneously. Continuing revenue must compound at 11%–12% CAGR over FY27–FY32 (reaching ~₹2,500+ Cr), and standalone EBITDA margins must expand by 250–350 bps from 11.0% toward 13.5%–14.5% [1][10]. Suppose margins stay pinned at 10.5%–11.0% and the effective tax rate normalizes to 25% (₹97.5 Cr PAT, ₹14.53 EPS). At a 14.5x bear multiple, intrinsic equity value drops to ₹211 per share (₹210.69 exact) [1][7].

web_blocks.takeaway: At the 2026-11-13 close of ₹311.30, base-case upside to ₹355 (+14.0%) is outweighed by a -32.2% bear-case risk to ₹211 (₹210.69 on tax-normalized EPS)—making patience for support critical [1][4].

web_blocks.caption: Specialty & Industrial Chemicals Peer Valuation Matrix (As of 2026-11-13)
web_blocks.takeaway: On true continuing earnings (18.5x headline / 21.4x tax-normalized P/E), INDIAGLYCO trades at or above Rossari Biotech (15.5x) and Galaxy Surfactants (18.7x–19.2x), while IG Petrochemicals (10.1x) offers a cheaper cyclical recovery multiple and Balaji Amines (25.7x) commands a premium for its 18.9% OPM [1][24][26].

web_blocks.html: The peer table reinforces our Reverse DCF conclusion [24][26]. Galaxy Surfactants (GALAXYSURF) trades at 18.7x–19.2x P/E with 30.2% TTM revenue growth and 13.5% ROCE [24]. Rossari Biotech (ROSSARI) trades at 15.5x P/E with 8.07% OPM and 13.3% ROCE [24]. IG Petrochemicals (IGPL) trades at 10.1x P/E in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend as phthalic anhydride spreads normalize [26]. Meanwhile, Balaji Amines (BALAMINES) trades at 25.7x P/E backed by an 18.86% operating margin [24]. INDIAGLYCO's 11.0% continuing OPM and 10.4% 3-year ROE do not warrant a 25x multiple today; its fair multiple is 17x–19x [1][4]. That means ₹311.30 (18.5x headline, 21.4x tax-normalized) already prices in operational recovery. The stock only becomes compelling on a pullback or if specialty margins expand ahead of schedule.

web_blocks.mechanism: Expanded via acquisitions and new capacity into surfactants, textile chemicals, and animal nutrition, but rising feedstock costs and commoditized product mix compressed operating margins from peak levels, triggering a multi-year valuation multiple de-rating.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: OPM compressed from ~17% in FY21 to 8.07% TTM by Nov 2026; P/E de-rated from >45x to 15.5x (MCap ₹2,426.82 Cr, CMP ₹427.15, -32.5% 1Y).
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Indian specialty chemical platforms with 8%–11% OPM and 11%–13% ROCE rarely sustain >20x multiples; INDIAGLYCO must lift BSPC margins toward 14% to avoid Rossari-style multiple compression [24].

web_blocks.html: A final valuation nuance involves the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals joint venture [11]. On the September 2026 balance sheet, total investments stand at ₹422 Cr [1][4]. In H1 FY27, the company booked ₹34 Cr in Other Income (₹21 Cr in Q1 and ₹13 Cr in Q2), reflecting treasury income and JV dividends/distributions. Even if we value the 49% JV stake separately at ~₹500–₹600 Cr (~1.2x–1.4x book carrying value) and subtract it alongside ₹422 Cr investments from Enterprise Value, the math stays tight. The core BSPC and Industrial Gases operating business still trades at 14.2x–16.0x annualized continuing EBITDA—reasonable for a de-leveraged green chemical asset, but hardly distressed [1][4][7].

Valuation & Action Trigger: We upgrade our posture from wait to buy only if price pulls back into the ₹269.72–₹277.94 support zone (~16.0x–16.5x continuing EPS) with a confirmed 4H turn, or if standalone continuing BSPC operating margins expand above 13.0% across Q3–Q4 FY27; conversely, a sustained margin drop below 9.5% or a close under ₹243.25 invalidates the base-case ₹355.00 valuation [1][23].

book_paragraphs: Whenever a company undergoes a major demerger, the financial data feeds you rely on every day become unreliable narrators for at least two quarters. At the November 13, 2026 ledger close of ₹311.30, India Glycols Limited carries a ₹2,086 crore market capitalization on 6.70 crore shares. Yet if you open Screener on its post-cutoff November 16 feed, it displays a ₹1,960 crore market cap at ₹292.45 and a headline price-to-earnings ratio of 9.27x—while TradingView shows an even lower 6.0x. On the surface, a single-digit multiple on a green specialty chemical manufacturer looks like a classic market oversight. You and I, however, know better than to trust an unadjusted trailing multiple after a corporate split.

Let us look closely at why that 9.27x figure is an illusion. Trailing twelve-month earnings as of September 2026 still carry two full pre-demerger quarters: the December 2025 quarter, when consolidated sales hit ₹1,102 crore and net profit reached ₹68 crore, and the March 2026 quarter, when sales were ₹976 crore and net profit was ₹87 crore. Those numbers were powered by the Potable Spirits and Bio-Fuels division—an engine that generated roughly 21% EBIT margins—and the Ennature Biopharma nutraceuticals business. Under the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement, effective September 1, 2026, both of those businesses have been carved out into separate entities.

What remains inside the listed shell of INDIAGLYCO is a much leaner, more focused chemical and industrial gases platform: the Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals division, the Industrial Gases business, and a 49% equity stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals. When we strip out the historical noise and look strictly at the two post-demerger quarters—Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27—a very different picture emerges. Revenue ran at ₹357 crore in the June quarter and ₹362 crore in the September quarter, giving us ₹719 crore for the half-year, or an annualized run-rate of ₹1,438 crore.

Operating profit in both quarters printed at exactly ₹39 crore, which translates to a standalone operating margin of 10.8% to 11.0%, or roughly ₹156 crore to ₹160 crore in annualized EBITDA. Below the operating line, the balance sheet cleanup is visible: quarterly interest expense dropped from ₹45–49 crore in the pre-demerger days down to ₹12 crore per quarter on the remaining ₹826 crore of debt. Other income, which includes treasury returns and upstreamed dividends from the Clariant joint venture, contributed ₹21 crore in Q1 and ₹13 crore in Q2—accounting for 52.3% of H1 FY27 pre-tax profit. After ₹12 crore in quarterly depreciation and an unusually low 12.31% effective tax rate, headline continuing net profit came in at ₹33 crore in Q1 and ₹24 crore in Q2—a total of ₹57 crore for the half-year, or ₹8.40 in half-year EPS.

Annualize that ₹8.40 half-year EPS and you get ₹16.80 per share, or ₹114 crore in headline annual continuing profit. At the November 13 close of ₹311.30, the headline continuing P/E ratio is 18.5x, not 9.27x. Better yet, if we apply a normalized 25% corporate tax rate to ₹130 crore of annualized pre-tax profit, normalized continuing profit drops to ₹97.5 crore—or ₹14.53 per share, which puts the true tax-normalized P/E at 21.42x. After adding ₹826 crore of debt and subtracting ₹422 crore of investments from the ₹2,086 crore market cap, Enterprise Value sits at ₹2,490 crore, or 14.2x to 16.0x continuing EBITDA.

To test whether ₹311.30 is a bargain or a fair-value trap, we run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow analysis. Using a 12% cost of equity and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, the ₹2,086 crore market capitalization implies that the continuing business must compound revenue at 11% to 12% annually over the next five years while expanding its standalone operating margin by 250 to 350 basis points—from 11% today toward 13.5% or 14.5%. That expansion is plausible if high-margin glycol ethers, green solvents, and Clariant JV dividends scale faster than commodity bio-MEG. But if margins stay pinned at 10.5% to 11.0% and tax normalizes to 25% (₹97.5 crore PAT, ₹14.53 EPS), a 14.5x bear multiple implies an intrinsic floor of ₹211 per share (₹210.69 exact).

Comparing INDIAGLYCO against its listed Indian chemical peers confirms this balanced reality. Galaxy Surfactants trades at 18.7x to 19.2x earnings with 30.2% trailing revenue growth and a 13.5% ROCE. Rossari Biotech, which suffered its own post-expansion margin compression down to 8.07% OPM, trades at 15.5x earnings. IG Petrochemicals trades at 10.1x earnings as phthalic anhydride spreads recover, while Balaji Amines commands 25.7x only because its operating margin sits at 18.86%. At 18.5x headline (21.4x tax-normalized) continuing earnings, INDIAGLYCO is priced at or above its peer pack—meaning that if you and I want an asymmetric return, we cannot pay full price on hope; we have to demand a discount to support.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the Enterprise Value and the Clariant JV Anchor
paragraphs: When you and I value a post-demerger industrial company, looking only at the price-to-earnings ratio can still leave a blind spot if the balance sheet carries significant debt or non-consolidated joint ventures. On September 30, 2026, India Glycols Limited reported total borrowings of ₹826 crore—down sharply from ₹1,691 crore in March 2026—alongside ₹422 crore of investments, the centerpiece of which is its 49% equity stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals.

If we start with the ₹2,086 crore market capitalization at the November 13 close of ₹311.30 per share, add ₹826 crore of debt, and subtract ₹422 crore of investments, we arrive at an adjusted Enterprise Value of ₹2,490 crore for the wholly owned Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals and Industrial Gases businesses. Against our annualized continuing EBITDA run-rate of ₹156 crore to ₹160 crore—or up to ₹175 crore if second-half utilization improves—the operating business trades at 14.2x to 16.0x EV/EBITDA.

To put that in context, an EV/EBITDA multiple between 14.2x and 16.0x is neither a distressed liquidation valuation nor a nosebleed growth multiple. It is the exact valuation zone where mature, capital-intensive specialty chemical producers trade when their return on capital employed sits in the 11% to 13% range. The reason why the market is not giving INDIAGLYCO a 20x or 25x EBITDA multiple today is straightforward: without the Potable Spirits business, standalone operating margins are sitting at 11.0%, and consolidated three-year ROE has averaged just 10.4%.

That brings us to the Clariant joint venture itself. Because Clariant holds 51% and operational control while INDIAGLYCO holds 49%, the JV's revenue is not consolidated line-by-line into INDIAGLYCO's top line; instead, INDIAGLYCO receives its share of profits and dividends, which helped lift Other Income to ₹21 crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹13 crore in Q2 FY27. Think of that JV stake as a stabilizing cash-flow anchor rather than a high-multiple hidden unicorn. Even if you assign ₹500 crore to ₹600 crore of equity value to the 49% Clariant stake, the implied multiple on the parent's Kashipur chemical assets still requires operational margin expansion to realize meaningful upside.

book_subsections.title: What the Reverse DCF Demands from Management Over FY27–FY32
paragraphs: In a traditional discounted cash flow model, an analyst plugs in optimistic growth assumptions and announces a target price. In a Reverse DCF, you and I flip the telescope around: we take the November 13 close of ₹311.30 and ask what the market is already forcing the company to achieve just to earn a normal 12% annual cost of equity.

Starting from ₹1,438 crore of annualized continuing revenue and an 11% operating margin, a 12% discount rate and 4.5% terminal growth rate require INDIAGLYCO to compound continuing revenue at 11% to 12% per year for the next five years—reaching roughly ₹2,500 crore by FY32—while simultaneously expanding operating margins from 11.0% toward 13.5% or 14.5%. That is a meaningful operational ask. It assumes that higher-margin green solvents, glycol ethers, and IGL-SteriGas medical/industrial gases grow much faster than commodity bio-MEG, and that crude-linked petrochemical MEG spreads do not undercut bio-based realizations.

Look at what happens in the downside case if those assumptions slip. Suppose crude oil prices soften and petrochemical MEG spreads stay depressed, pinning INDIAGLYCO's operating margin at 10.5% to 11.0% while revenue grows at 7.5% and the effective tax rate normalizes to 25% on ₹130 crore of pre-tax profit. In that environment, normalized net profit sits at ₹97.5 crore (₹14.53 per share), a 14.5x bear multiple implies a ₹211 per share floor (₹210.69 exact)—a 32.2% drawdown from ₹311.30. Conversely, if management executes on specialty mix, leverages the halved ₹12 crore quarterly interest bill, and grows continuing PAT toward ₹155 crore by FY29, an 18.5x multiple yields ₹355 per share in our base case, and ₹420 in a bull case where the market re-rates the cleaner balance sheet to 21x.

book_subsections.title: Peer Cross-Check: Why Specialty Multiples Are Earned, Not Given
paragraphs: Comparing INDIAGLYCO directly against four listed Indian chemical peers—Galaxy Surfactants, Rossari Biotech, IG Petrochemicals, and Balaji Amines—removes any remaining ambiguity about where ₹311.30 sits on the valuation spectrum. Galaxy Surfactants trades at 18.7x to 19.2x earnings with 30.2% trailing revenue growth and a 13.5% ROCE. Rossari Biotech trades at 15.5x earnings after its operating margin compressed to 8.07%. IG Petrochemicals trades at 10.1x earnings as a pure cyclical phthalic anhydride recovery play, while Balaji Amines trades at 25.7x earnings thanks to an 18.86% operating margin.

Notice the pattern across all four peers: the market pays a mid-teens multiple for 8% to 11% operating margins, and reserves 25x+ multiples for businesses generating high-teens margins and >20% capital returns. At 18.5x headline (21.4x tax-normalized) continuing earnings and an 11% operating margin, INDIAGLYCO is already priced at or above Galaxy Surfactants and Rossari Biotech. There is no free lunch at ₹311.30—which is why our technical discipline in the next chapter becomes decisive.

book_subsections.title: Walkthrough: Why Screener's 9.27x P/E and TradingView's 6.0x P/E Mislead
paragraphs: Let us walk through the exact arithmetic of how data aggregators produce conflicting multiples right after a demerger, because understanding this mechanism will protect you on every future corporate spin-off you study. On Screener, the trailing twelve-month net profit is calculated by summing the last four reported consolidated quarters: December 2025 (₹68 crore), March 2026 (₹87 crore), June 2026 (₹33 crore), and September 2026 (₹24 crore). Add those four numbers together and you get ₹212 crore of reported TTM profit. On Screener's post-cutoff November 16 snapshot (₹1,960 crore market cap at ₹292.45), dividing by ₹212 crore produces a Stock P/E of 9.27x (or ~9.8x on the ₹2,086 crore market cap at our November 13 close of ₹311.30).

TradingView goes one step further in creating confusion: its automated feed displays a trailing P/E of 6.0x because its trailing EPS still reflects an older pre-demerger and pre-split/preferential-adjustment base. Both numbers share the same fatal flaw: they treat ₹155 crore of combined profit from the December 2025 and March 2026 quarters as if it still belongs to today's shareholders of INDIAGLYCO.

In reality, the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement transferred the Potable Spirits and Bio-Fuels undertaking into IGL Spirits Limited and the Nutraceuticals undertaking into Ennature Bio Pharma Limited, effective September 1, 2026 with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2026. That is why Q1 FY27 (June 2026) and Q2 FY27 (September 2026) were reported strictly on the continuing perimeter. When you annualize the ₹57 crore of net profit earned across those two continuing quarters—₹33 crore in Q1 and ₹24 crore in Q2—you get ₹114 crore of headline continuing earnings, or ₹16.80 per share across 6.70 crore shares. At ₹311.30, that is 18.5x headline earnings, and 21.42x on our tax-normalized ₹97.5 crore (₹14.53 EPS) baseline—more than double Screener's headline 9.27x.

This same perimeter discipline applies to the balance sheet. In March 2026, total consolidated assets stood at ₹6,523 crore, backed by ₹4,554 crore of fixed assets and ₹1,691 crore of borrowings. By September 2026, total assets reset to ₹2,611 crore, fixed assets reset to ₹1,257 crore (plus ₹114 crore of capital work-in-progress), and borrowings halved to ₹826 crore. Equity reserves also adjusted from ₹2,899 crore down to ₹1,224 crore as the demerged net assets moved out to the new entities. Book value per share on Screener sits at ₹188, meaning the stock at ₹311.30 trades at roughly 1.66x post-demerger book value—a sensible, unstretched multiple for an 11% ROE business, yet far from the deep-value bargain that 9.27x P/E implies.

Finally, consider the tax rate and other income line items in Q1 and Q2 FY27. Effective tax printed at just 12.31% across H1 FY27, while Other Income contributed ₹34 crore—or 52.3% of the ₹65 crore half-year pre-tax profit. Part of that lower tax rate reflects dividend income from the Clariant JV and demerger transition adjustments. If the effective tax rate normalizes to 25% on ₹130 crore of annualized pre-tax profit, normalized PAT drops to ₹97.5 crore (₹14.53 EPS), lifting the P/E at ₹311.30 to 21.42x. Standalone operating profit will therefore need to rise from ₹39 crore per quarter toward ₹48–₹52 crore per quarter just to hold continuing net profit steady above ₹115 crore.

book_subsections.title: Working Capital, Debt Service Coverage, and Sum-of-the-Parts Sanity Check
paragraphs: Another way to stress-test our ₹355 base target and ₹211 bear case is to look at debt service coverage and working-capital intensity on the new post-demerger balance sheet. At ₹826 crore of borrowings and ₹12 crore of quarterly interest expense—₹48 crore annualized—INDIAGLYCO's implied cost of debt sits near 5.8% to 6.0% on ending debt, or roughly 6% to 7% depending on average intra-quarter utilization and working-capital limits. Against ₹156 crore to ₹160 crore of annualized standalone EBITDA and ₹60 crore to ₹68 crore of annualized other income, interest coverage sits at roughly 4.5x on combined EBITDA plus other income, or 3.3x on standalone operating profit alone—where ₹48 crore interest consumes 30.8% of standalone EBITDA.

That improvement is real, yet it also shows why we cannot treat INDIAGLYCO as a debt-free compounder. Gross debt of ₹826 crore is still 5.29x standalone continuing EBITDA, and total working capital—other assets of ₹819 crore minus other liabilities of ₹527 crore, or ₹292 crore net—absorbs roughly 20% of annualized continuing sales. In specialty chemicals, every incremental ₹100 crore of revenue requires roughly ₹20 crore of incremental working capital alongside maintenance and debottlenecking capex.

If we run a quick Sum-of-the-Parts sanity check on the continuing company, the picture aligns almost identically with our Reverse DCF. Value the wholly owned BSPC and Industrial Gases operating business at 10x to 11x FY28E EBITDA of ₹175 crore—which gives ₹1,750 crore to ₹1,925 crore of Enterprise Value—add ₹450 crore to ₹550 crore for the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals joint venture stake, and subtract ₹826 crore of debt. That lands equity value between ₹1,374 crore and ₹1,649 crore on conservative multiples (₹205 to ₹246 per share), rising toward ₹2,200 crore to ₹2,400 crore (₹328 to ₹358 per share) once EBITDA scales toward ₹200 crore and debt continues paying down. Everything points to the same conclusion: ₹311.30 is rich on current earnings, while ₹269.72–₹277.94 is where the odds tilt in your favor.

book_subsections.title: Historical Parallel: Rossari Biotech and the Specialty Margin Ceiling
paragraphs: To ground that multiple ceiling in real Indian market history, look closely at Rossari Biotech between 2021 and November 2026. Five years ago, Rossari was celebrated as a high-growth specialty chemical compounder and commanded a price-to-earnings ratio north of 45x on expectations of sustained high-teens operating margins. Yet as the company expanded across surfactants, textile chemicals, and animal nutrition amid rising raw-material volatility, operating margins compressed from roughly 17% down to 8.07% on a trailing twelve-month basis. By November 2026, Rossari's stock had fallen 32.5% over the prior year to ₹427.15, and its P/E multiple had de-rated all the way to 15.5x on a ₹2,426.82 crore market cap.

The lesson for India Glycols Limited is unmistakable. Investors often assume that simply shedding a legacy conglomerate structure automatically entitles a chemical business to a 25x or 30x specialty multiple. In reality, Indian chemical multiples follow operating margins and return on capital employed, not corporate-structure slides. Until INDIAGLYCO proves it can lift continuing BSPC operating margins from 11.0% toward 13.5% or 14.0% and push ROE well above its 10.4% three-year average, 17x to 19x continuing earnings is the rational valuation ceiling.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Anchor on a Pre-Demerger Multiple
book_callouts.text: The single easiest mistake in special-situations investing is letting a screener's trailing P/E do your thinking for you. When two-thirds of a company's revenue and its highest-margin liquor division walk out the door, a 9.27x trailing P/E is a ghost of the past. Stripping the P&L down to ₹1,438 crore of continuing revenue, ₹114 crore of headline PAT, and ₹97.5 crore of tax-normalized PAT reveals an 18.5x headline (21.4x normalized) multiple at ₹311.30—meaning our entry discipline has to do the heavy lifting.
